_comment: Reference DATA for WebPivot/tools/wp_google.py — the GHunt (github.com/mxrch/GHunt) wrapper that turns an email address or Gaia ID into Google-account LEADS. Edit here, not in Python: the binary names, the session-file locations whose PRESENCE means `ghunt login` was done (contents are never read), the setup steps shown when it is missing, the keyless URL templates, the user-type -> account-kind map and the per-field caveats. Every output value is a lead (SKILL.md RULE 5), never a KB edge or an operator link.

settings._comment: GHunt owns authenticated HTTP transport (including its Google-client user agents and proxy behaviour); the wrapper makes no direct HTTP requests. timeout_seconds bounds one subprocess run; bin_env optionally selects a GHunt executable, never a credential.

binaries._comment: Executable names looked up on PATH, in order, when GHUNT_BIN is unset. If none is found but the `ghunt` Python package is importable in this interpreter it is run as `python -c 'from ghunt.ghunt import main; main()'`.

session_files._comment: Where `ghunt login` stores the analyst's own research-account session (GHuntCreds default: ~/.malfrats/ghunt/creds.m). Only existence and non-zero size are checked — the file is NEVER opened, read, copied or printed, and no cookie/token is ever accepted as an argument.

setup._comment: Shown verbatim in the `skipped` result when GHunt is not installed or has no session. The login step must use the analyst's dedicated research Google account, never a personal or client account.
values: pipx install ghunt   (or: uv tool install ghunt)
ghunt login   (sign in with the analyst's dedicated research Google account — GHunt's own login flow; never paste cookies into this tool)

endpoints._comment: Keyless URL templates built from a Gaia ID / email / name. They are emitted as links for the analyst to open; this tool does not fetch them. {gaia}, {email} and {q} are URL-encoded before substitution.

account_kinds._comment: People-API userTypes (as GHunt returns them) mapped to an account kind. Workspace wins when any workspace type, a Chat customerId or isEntrepriseUser is present; unknown types fall through to `unknown`.

caveats._comment: Per-lead caveat text attached to each emitted lead (RULE 5: every Google-account datum is a lead to corroborate, not an attribution). Keys are the lead types wp_google.py emits.

entries.overall: Google-account data is a LEAD (RULE 5), not proof of who operates an account. Missing or skipped data does not prove an account exists or is absent. Never add it as a KB edge or operator link without independent corroboration.
entries.gaia_id: Stable Google account identifier for this address at lookup time; one person can hold many accounts and an address can be re-pointed.
entries.profile_name: Self-declared display name — anyone can type any name.
entries.profile_photo: A custom photo may be a stock, borrowed or AI image; reverse-search before treating it as the account holder's face.
entries.cover_photo: Self-chosen image; same caution as the profile photo.
entries.last_profile_edit: Last time the PROFILE container changed (photo/name), not last login or last activity.
entries.maps_contrib: A Maps review or photo shows a place the account VISITED (or claims to), not a residence or workplace; clusters suggest a region, not an address.
entries.maps_stats: Public contribution counts only; private contributions are invisible, so zero is not proof of inactivity.
entries.calendar: A public calendar exposes what the owner chose to publish; event titles can be shared or imported, not necessarily attended.
entries.play_games: Play Games profiles are often auto-created with a random gamertag; a name or avatar here is self-chosen.
entries.youtube: Name-search guess only — Google exposes no gaia->channel link; any channel matching the name is unverified.
entries.services: Services the account can be reached on (in-app reachability), not proof of active use.
entries.workspace_customer: A Workspace customer ID identifies the tenant (organisation), not the person; two addresses sharing it share an employer/tenant, which is itself only a lead.
